title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f81v shared enclosure names concurrent occupants or successive treatment stages
summary: The already admitted V70 visual inventory owns f81v as one enclosure with two figure rows and two complete prose blocks above it; the rows are not separately owned basins or records (IDEA647 decision). Freeze that single-enclosure geometry and both complete block boundaries before reading words. Compare a concurrent reading in which the blocks describe distinct occupants or conditions of one shared place with a sequential reading in which the same participant changes treatment state between blocks. A sequential complete reading must supply an overt, independently constrained same-participant reference and directional temporal change, while the concurrent rival must account for both rows without inventing a handoff. Check every content-bearing span across ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b and retain all unassigned material. This is a raw hypothesis, not a claim that the rows are two records or that any word means bath, person, or stage; no semantic test is authorized by the picture alone.

design.mechanism: A complete f81v reading binds the page's two prose blocks to one pictured enclosure and distinguishes concurrent occupants from a before-and-after state of one participant.
design.unit: The two complete admitted f81v prose blocks and the single visually owned enclosure containing two figure rows.
design.contrast: Concurrent different occupants or conditions in a shared enclosure versus successive states of one retained participant.
design.prediction: Only the successive-state account requires a cross-block participant identity plus an explicit ordered change; a fully specified reading lacking either must choose the concurrent account or leave the contrast unresolved. The concurrent account must identify how both figure rows fit one enclosure without assigning separate basins or textual owners.
